In  [[mathematics]], more specifically [[sheaf theory]], a branch of [[topology]] and [[algebraic geometry]], the '''exceptional inverse image functor''' is the fourth and most sophisticated in a series of [[image functors for sheaves]]. It is needed to express [[Verdier duality]] in its most general form.

==Definition==
{{Images of sheaves}}
Let ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'' be a [[continuous map]] of [[topological spaces]] or a [[morphism]] of [[scheme (mathematics)|schemes]]. Then the exceptional inverse image is a functor
:R''f''<sup>!</sup>: D(''Y'') → D(''X'')
where D(–) denotes the [[derived category]] of [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] of abelian groups or modules over a fixed ring.

It is defined to be the [[adjoint functor|right adjoint]] of the [[derived functor|total derived functor]] R''f''<sub>!</sub> of the [[direct image with compact support]]. Its existence follows from certain properties of R''f''<sub>!</sub> and general theorems about existence of adjoint functors, as does the unicity.

The notation R''f''<sup>!</sup> is an abuse of notation insofar as there is in general no functor ''f''<sup>!</sup> whose derived functor would be R''f''<sup>!</sup>.

==Examples and properties==
*If ''f'': ''X'' → ''Y'' is an [[Immersion (mathematics)|immersion]] of a [[locally closed]] subspace, then it is possible to define

::''f''<sup>!</sup>(''F'') := ''f''<sup>∗</sup> ''G'',

:where ''G'' is the subsheaf of ''F'' of which the sections on some open subset ''U'' of ''Y'' are the sections ''s'' ∈ ''F''(''U'') whose [[support (mathematics)|support]] is contained in ''X''. The functor ''f''<sup>!</sup> is [[left exact functor|left exact]], and the above R''f''<sup>!</sup>, whose existence is guaranteed by [[abstract nonsense]], is indeed the derived functor of this ''f''<sup>!</sup>. Moreover ''f''<sup>!</sup> is right adjoint to [[direct image with compact support|''f''<sub>!</sub>]], too.
 
*Slightly more generally, a similar statement holds for any [[quasi-finite morphism]] such as an [[étale morphism]].
*If ''f'' is an [[open immersion]], the exceptional inverse image equals the usual [[inverse image functor|inverse image]].

==Duality of the exceptional inverse image functor==
Let <math>X</math> be a smooth manifold of dimension <math>d</math> and let <math>f: X \rightarrow *</math> be the unique map which maps everything to one point. For a ring <math>\Lambda</math>, one finds that <math>f^{!} \Lambda=\omega_{X, \Lambda}[d]</math> is the shifted <math>\Lambda</math>-[[orientation sheaf]].

On the other hand, let <math>X</math> be a smooth <math>k</math>-variety of dimension <math>d</math>. If <math>f: X \rightarrow \operatorname{Spec}(k)</math> denotes the structure morphism then <math>f^{!} k \cong \omega_{X}[d]</math> is the shifted [[Canonical bundle|canonical sheaf]] on <math>X</math>.

Moreover, let <math>X</math> be a smooth <math>k</math>-variety of dimension <math>d</math> and <math>\ell</math> a prime invertible in <math>k</math>. Then <math>f^{!} \mathbb{Q}_{\ell} \cong \mathbb{Q}_{\ell}(d)[2 d]</math> where <math>(d)</math> denotes the [[Tate twist]].

Recalling the definition of the compactly supported cohomology as [[Direct image with compact support|lower-shriek pushforward]] and noting that below the last <math>\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}</math> means the constant sheaf on <math>X</math> and the rest mean that on <math>*</math>, <math>f:X\to *</math>, and
:: <math>\mathrm{H}_{c}^{n}(X)^{*} \cong \operatorname{Hom}\left(f_! f^{*} \mathbb{Q}_{\ell}[n], \mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\right) \cong \operatorname{Hom}\left(\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}, f_{*} f^{!} \mathbb{Q}_{\ell}[-n]\right),</math>
the above computation furnishes the <math>\ell</math>-adic [[Poincaré duality]]
:: <math>\mathrm{H}_{c}^{n}\left(X ; \mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\right)^{*} \cong \mathrm{H}^{2 d-n}(X ; \mathbb{Q}(d))</math>
from the repeated application of the adjunction condition.
